domain: RTS/RPG squad movement — steering, formation settling, 360° security halts, procedural "alive" polish — for a deterministic headless infantry sim (units = meters, cellSize 5 m). Variation must be derived from the stable unit id + sim.timeS, never per-frame RNG, so replays stay bit-exact.
paramTargets: Ring slot radius: KLE 14 m / default 20 m (unchanged), min angular sep = 2*asin(2.5/radius) rad floor 0.35 rad. Per-soldier spacing 4.5-5.5 m within team; inter-team gap 11-14 m with SL between (down from 18). Arrival deadband: stop micro-correcting inside 1.4 m of slot, "settled" hysteresis 1.4 m enter / 2.6 m exit. Facing slew cap: 160-200 deg/s moving, 70-90 deg/s at halt (kills 729 deg/s dither). Idle scan: +/-18-28 deg sinusoid, period 6-11 s, deterministic from id. Personality magnitudes: spacing *0.88..1.12, pace *0.93..1.07, reaction lag 0.0..0.35 s, settle radial offset +/-0.6 m, settle tangential +/-12 deg. Decision phase stagger: hash(id)%cadence so re-plans don't align. Hard de-overlap at halt: min center-center 1.1 m (2*BODY), push apart 0.5*overlap each.
pitfalls: 1) Don't add Math.random() or draw from sim.rng inside per-tick movement — it desyncs replays; use RNG.hashString(u.id) (a pure function, advances no stream) mixed with quantized sim.timeS. 2) Don't rate-limit facing without a deadband AND hysteresis — a slew cap alone still hunts forever around the target angle and re-creates dither at low amplitude. 3) Don't run Hungarian/O(n^3) assignment per tick on the ring — assign ONCE on entry to holdSecurity and cache slot->id on the Task; re-running every tick lets two men swap targets and oscillate. 4) Don't resolve hard overlap by teleporting — clamp the per-tick push so two stacked men ease apart over a few ticks, or they visibly pop. 5) Per-agent pace personality must be applied as a multiplier on the FOLLOWER's target spacing / the slot offset, NOT on the navigator's throttle, or the whole column inherits one man's slowness. 6) Idle sway must freeze the instant faceLock changes to a real threat bearing (combat), or men "look away" from contact. 7) The min-angular-sep clamp on the ring must not push a slot onto impassable ground — re-snap with passTarget after de-confliction. 8) Keep the deadband below the path-arrival epsilon interactions: moveUnit shifts a waypoint at d<1.2 m, so a settle deadband must be >=1.2 m or the man never "arrives" and keeps the path non-empty.

principles.title: Bearing-optimal ring assignment so nobody crosses the circle
principles.realityOrCraft: A squad setting up a 360 doesn't send a man to the far arc through the middle of everyone — each soldier peels to the NEAREST open sector. Good RTS games solve this as a min-total-rotation assignment (cheap Hungarian / greedy nearest-bearing) computed once on the halt, then held.
principles.currentGap: holdSecurity() in formation.ts:225-239 lays men by RAW MEMBER INDEX: a=(i/n)*2π+0.4. The roster order has no relation to where men physically are, so a man on the near side is routinely told to walk to the opposite arc, crossing the whole element — the exact 'stuck on each other at the 360' the user flagged. No assignment, no de-confliction.
principles.change: Rewrite holdSecurity to: (1) build n candidate slot angles a_k=(k/n)*2π (drop the +0.4 fixed offset). (2) Greedy nearest-bearing assignment: for each man compute his current bearing from center = atan2(pos.y-cy,pos.x-cx); sort men by bearing; rotate the slot ring to the offset that minimizes summed |angleDiff(manBearing, slotBearing)| (try all n rotations of the sorted-vs-sorted pairing — O(n^2)=81 ops for 9 men, trivial). Assign each man the slot at his rank. This is optimal for points on a circle (no crossings) and far cheaper than Hungarian. (3) Enforce min angular sep: if two final slots are closer than MIN_SEP=max(0.35, 2*asin(2.5/radius)) rad, spread them. (4) Cache the slotId->memberId map on the Task (t.ringSlots) and REUSE it on re-entry (releaseCombat re-securing) so men don't reshuffle every time contact flickers. Snap each final slot with passTarget(w,...) so none land in the wire/cliff.
principles.params: a_k=(k/n)*2π; MIN_SEP=max(0.35 rad, 2*asin(2.5/radius)); radius 14 (kle)/20. Assignment cost = Σ|angleDiff|. Cache key t.ringSlots:{[memberId]:angle}.
principles.risk: Could regress if a man's near-bearing slot is on impassable ground; mitigate with passTarget re-snap + fallback to next-nearest open slot. Verify: add a 'ring crossing' metric to scripts/cohesion.ts (count member-paths whose straight segment to slot passes within 3 m of another member) — expect near-zero after, and watch blocked% at the onstation transition drop.

principles.title: Arrival ease-in + settle deadband to kill the 729 deg/s halt dither
principles.realityOrCraft: A man arriving at his spot decelerates into it and then STOPS fidgeting — he doesn't micro-correct his heading 100x/s. The dither metric (729 deg/s) is a body re-solving a sub-meter error every tick.
principles.currentGap: moveUnit (combat.ts:606-617) shifts a waypoint at d<1.2 and zeroes speed, but facing is still recomputed from a near-zero goalDir each tick (combat.ts:652) and holdSecurity hands a fresh path whenever dist>2 (formation.ts:238), so a man parked 1.3-2.5 m off his slot keeps getting a new 1-waypoint path and re-aims — perpetual twitch. There is no 'close enough, settle' state.
principles.change: Add a settle state with hysteresis. In holdSecurity/driveFollower, when dist(pos,slot) < SETTLE_IN (1.4 m): clear u.path=[], set a u.settled=true flag, and STOP issuing new paths until dist exceeds SETTLE_OUT (2.6 m). While settled, do NOT recompute facing from motion — hold faceLock (see facing-slew item). Add a speed ease-in: in moveUnit, when within ARRIVE_EASE=4 m of the final waypoint, scale speed by smoothstep(0.5,1, d/ARRIVE_EASE) so the last few meters decelerate instead of full-speed-then-stop (smoothstep already in rng.ts).
principles.params: SETTLE_IN=1.4 m, SETTLE_OUT=2.6 m (>path epsilon 1.2 m so 'arrived' is stable), ARRIVE_EASE=4 m, ease floor 0.5×.
principles.risk: Deadband too large could leave men visibly out of line; 1.4 m is below the 5 m spacing so the ring still reads tight. Verify: cohesion.ts jitter (deg/s) should fall from 729 spike toward <60; add a 'settled-twitch' sub-metric = mean |dHeading| for members with speed<0.1.

principles.title: Rate-limited facing (slew) + idle scan/sway instead of instantaneous snap
principles.realityOrCraft: Heads and torsos turn at a finite rate; troops at a halt slowly scan their sector, they don't lock rigid like turrets. Both the smooth turn and the gentle scan are what read as 'alive'.
principles.currentGap: combat.ts:652 sets u.facing = faceLock ?? angle(dir) — an instantaneous snap. When faceLock flips (e.g. ring assignment, or a turn in the column) facing teleports; at halt it's frozen dead-still (halt() at combat.ts:703 hard-sets u.facing=u.faceLock). Both read robotic and the snap is a chunk of the jitter metric.
principles.change: Replace the two hard sets with a slew toward the target. Compute targetFace = faceLock!=null ? faceLock : angle(dir). Then u.facing += clamp(angleDiff(u.facing,targetFace), -rate*dt, +rate*dt) where rate = MOVING_SLEW (3.0 rad/s ≈170°/s) when moving, HALT_SLEW (1.4 rad/s ≈80°/s) when halted. At a security halt, add a deterministic idle scan: targetFace += scanAmp*sin(2π*(timeS/scanPeriod + phase)), with scanAmp, scanPeriod, phase derived from hash(u.id) (see personality item) — amp 0.32 rad (~18°), period 7-11 s. Freeze the scan (scanAmp→0) whenever u.targetId or threatDir is set so men snap attention to real contact. Apply in combat.ts moveUnit AND halt().
principles.params: MOVING_SLEW=3.0 rad/s, HALT_SLEW=1.4 rad/s, scanAmp=0.28-0.40 rad, scanPeriod=7-11 s, phase=hashUnit01(id)*2π. Uses angleDiff (vec.ts:76).
principles.risk: Slew during fast column turns could lag facing behind heading and look like skating; 170°/s covers a 90° turn in ~0.5 s which is fine at patrol pace. Scan must freeze in contact (gate on targetId/threatDir) or men look away from the enemy. Verify: cohesion jitter drops; eyeball via Playwright at a halt that heads sway, not jerk.

principles.title: Deterministic per-agent personality from id-hash
principles.realityOrCraft: No two soldiers hold exactly the same interval, pace, or reaction time. Tiny stable per-man variation (a half-meter looser, a beat slower to react, settling a few degrees off the geometric slot) is the single biggest 'these are people not clones' lever, and games bake it from a per-entity seed.
principles.currentGap: Every follower uses the identical plan.spacing, identical slot geometry, identical instant reaction. driveFollower (formation.ts:446) and squadSlots (formation.ts:288) are perfectly uniform — the formation reads as a rigid lattice.
principles.change: Add a pure helper personality(id) in formation.ts (or a shared util) that returns stable scalars from h=RNG.hashString(id) (rng.ts:14 — pure, advances no stream): split h into bytes for independent axes. Apply: (a) per-man spacing mult = 0.88+0.24*r1 on his slot back/lat offsets in driveFollower; (b) settle offset: radial ±0.6 m and tangential ±12° added to his ring slot in holdSecurity (so the circle isn't geometrically perfect); (c) reaction lag: a per-man re-aim/re-path delay of 0..0.35 s (see desync item); (d) pace mult 0.93..1.07 applied to the follower's catch-up target spacing only (NOT the navigator throttle). Keep magnitudes small so doctrine still reads.
principles.params: hashUnit01(id)=RNG.hashString(id)/2^32. spacing×[0.88,1.12], settle radial ±0.6 m, settle tangential ±0.21 rad, reactionLag [0,0.35] s, pace×[0.93,1.07]. 3-4 independent axes from different byte-shifts of the hash.
principles.risk: Spacing variation could open the file past a choke; it's only ±12% of an already-tightened 5 m, well within corridor clamps in driveFollower (formation.ts:470-478). Determinism: hashString is pure, so replays stay bit-exact — verify by running cohesion.ts twice on a seed and diffing output (must be identical).

principles.title: Hard minimum-separation resolve at the halt (no two men on one point)
principles.realityOrCraft: Bodies can't occupy the same ground. Local steering separation eases crowding while MOVING, but once men stop steering (halted, path empty) nothing keeps two settling men from converging on overlapping points.
principles.currentGap: steer() in steering.ts only runs inside moveUnit when a unit has a path (combat.ts:648). A man with path=[] (settled/holding) gets NO separation — halt() at combat.ts:699 just stops him. Two ring slots placed close (or two men settling from the same side) can end up <1 m apart and visually interpenetrate, the stacking the user sees at the 360.
principles.change: Add a cheap hard de-overlap pass for HALTED/holding units, run once per tick after movement (e.g. in CombatSim.tick after the move loop, or in moveUnit's halt path). For each halted unit, query neighborsFor(u) (combat.ts:563, already bucketed) and for any non-hostile neighbor with center-center d < MIN_BODY=1.1 m (2*BODY, BODY=0.55 from steering.ts:38), push each apart by 0.5*(MIN_BODY-d) along the separation axis, clamped to MAX_PUSH=0.25 m/tick so they ease apart over ~3-4 ticks instead of popping, and only into passable cells (reuse the passableCell guard from moveUnit:660). Deterministic (pure geometry, no RNG).
principles.params: MIN_BODY=1.1 m, push=0.5*(MIN_BODY-d) per man, MAX_PUSH=0.25 m/tick, passable-guarded. Applies to units with path.length===0 || formationHold || brainState in {holding,onstation}.
principles.risk: Could fight the ring assignment if slots are legitimately <1.1 m (only at tiny radius / many men) — the MIN_SEP ring clamp (item 1) prevents that. Pushing into the wire is guarded. Verify: add 'min pairwise dist among members' to cohesion.ts at the onstation frame — expect it to rise to ~1.1 m floor and never go below.

principles.title: Stagger decision/re-plan phase so the squad doesn't think in lockstep
principles.realityOrCraft: Real squads desync naturally — men react on their own beat. When every agent re-plans on the same tick the whole formation lurches together (a visible synchronized stutter) and re-path cost spikes.
principles.currentGap: steerSquad (formation.ts:139-152) drives EVERY follower every tick from the same nav update, and the only existing throttles (friendly brainTimer 0.4-0.7 s at friendly.ts:31, perceptTimer at combat.ts:321) are seeded from sim.rng.next() — fine for determinism but uniform in phase, so reactions can bunch. There's no per-unit phase offset on the formation re-aim.
principles.change: Give each follower a deterministic decision PHASE so their catch-up re-paths and the reactionLag (item 4) are spread across the tick window. In driveFollower, gate the expensive re-path branch (formation.ts:490-498 findPath) behind a per-unit phase: only re-path on ticks where floor((timeS+phaseOff)/REPLAN_PERIOD) increments, phaseOff = hashUnit01(id)*REPLAN_PERIOD. Cheap wake-following still runs every tick (it's just spacing); only the A* rejoin is phased. This both desyncs the visual lurch and amortizes pathfinding. Also apply reactionLag as a delay before a follower starts reacting to a new nav heading (hold previous slot target for reactionLag seconds).
principles.params: REPLAN_PERIOD=0.5 s, phaseOff=hashUnit01(id)*0.5 s. reactionLag from item 4 (0..0.35 s). Only gates the findPath rejoin, never the per-tick wake bead.
principles.risk: Phasing the rejoin could briefly delay a genuinely-wedged man's re-route by up to 0.5 s — negligible vs the existing STALL_WINDOW=2 s (combat.ts:171). Verify cohesion.ts lenCV (accordion) doesn't worsen and blocked% holds; check reachT unchanged.

principles.title: Tighten spacing to doctrine (5 m men, 11-14 m teams, SL between)
principles.realityOrCraft: Doctrinal foot-patrol interval is ~5 m between individual soldiers and ~10-15 m between fire teams/squads, with the squad leader positioned BETWEEN the two teams to control both.
principles.currentGap: planFormation (formation.ts:58) sets patrol interval = 9 m (nearly double doctrine) and squadSlots (formation.ts:292) sets inter-team gap = max(interval*2,14) ≈ 18 m — both too wide, which both spreads the element thin (worsening the accordion/lenCV up to 0.63) and is part of why paceEff reads low (longer file = more lag = more governor braking).
principles.change: In planFormation, retune the technique spacing ladder so patrol≈5: e.g. crawl 3, concealed 4, tactical 4.5, patrol 5, traveling 6, rush 7 (keep the expect×1.3 and restrictive×0.72 modifiers; clamp 3.5..12 instead of 3.5..20). In squadSlots, set gap = clamp(interval*2.4, 11, 14) so teams sit 11-14 m apart, and confirm the SL slot (formation.ts:298, back:gap) lands BETWEEN lead team and trail team (trail team at gap*1.8 → SL at ~0.55 of the way back, which is between — good; verify with new numbers).
principles.params: patrol interval 5 m (was 9); inter-team gap clamp [11,14] (was max(×2,14)≈18); per-man within-team = interval. Overall spacing clamp [3.5,12].
principles.risk: Tighter spacing raises crowding → more separation steering work and slightly higher stack risk at chokes; the hard de-overlap (item 5) and corridor clamp absorb it. Verify: cohesion.ts lenCV should drop (shorter, steadier file) and paceEff should RISE (less lag → less governor braking, addressing the 0.35 baseline); confirm blocked% doesn't climb at the gate.
